nextStoryContext: All 31 test/integration/**/*.test.ts files carrying a join(tmpdir() rooting spelling (44 occurrences, incl. the bare sentinel path at plan-runner-pane-spawn.test.ts:161) are migrated onto createTestTmpdir via scripts/codemod-test-tmpdir.ts, matching the PRD's informative reference exactly. One codemod invocation covering all 31 files rewrote every site in one pass with zero hand-edits, BUT bun run typecheck surfaced a NEW (4th) codemod edge case beyond the US-004 pair: test/integration/dispatch-oversize-prompt.test.ts's stripQuotedStringLiteralContents usage-check scanner misread a literal single-quote embedded in a backtick template literal's STATIC text (a shell-quoting helper: `` `'${value.replace(/'/g, "'\\''")}'` ``) as opening a new single-quoted string, which then swallowed real code (including a later, live join(root, '.claude') call) until it happened to find a closing quote several lines away -- causing the still-used `import { join } from 'node:path';` to be wrongly pruned. Root-cause fixed in scripts/codemod-test-tmpdir.ts (US-003's shared, committed codemod): stripQuotedStringLiteralContents now has a dedicated backtick-tracked branch (consumeTemplateLiteral, split into consumeTemplateStaticSegment + consumeTemplateInterpolation to stay under the repo's cognitive-complexity lint ceiling of 15) that copies a whole template literal through untouched, char-for-char, brace-depth-counting `${...}` interpolations, without ever treating an embedded quote character as a string delimiter. Regression-pinned with a new test in test/codemod-test-tmpdir.test.ts (18/18 pass, up from 17). Detection method unchanged from prior fronts: bun run typecheck surfaces an unpruned-but-dead OR wrongly-pruned-but-live import immediately as TS6133/TS2304. GOTCHA 10 re-check swept across all three axes for test/integration: (a)/(b) four files (gitignore-implement-blocked-marker, issue-file-spec-channel, journal-append-on-main, triage-real-git) do their own real `git init` inside the scratch dir via node:child_process's spawnSync, which -- unlike Bun.spawnSync/Bun.spawn (see the US-003 GOTCHA 10(b) sharpening bullet) -- inherits live process.env including a runtime GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES mutation by default, so that gotcha does not apply here; all four passed cleanly in isolation and in the full suite. (c) no absolute-path-prefix, pane-title, or tmux-cwd assertion anywhere in the touched subtree keys off the scratch dir's path shape or length (checked dashboard-pane-selfspawn, ensure-worker-pane-selfheal, plan-runner-pane-spawn/no-prd/target-obey, orch-recycle-watch/pid-resolve, orch-respawn-reresolve, orch-exit-preserves-state, sidecar-liveness-watch-fd-leak, stop-sidecar-real/defaultlistprocesses-real, sync-worktree-on-main, supervisor-outcome-cam58, self-invoke-compiled -- zero hits). Full bun test: 6047 pass / 0 fail (up from prior baseline; includes the real-tmux and real-git integration tests genuinely unskipped, not gated out). file-size-budget.json needed NO raise this story (bun run check:all's file-size gate passed clean with no changes, despite scripts/codemod-test-tmpdir.ts growing by ~65 net lines for the new branch/helpers). Remaining rooting sites are US-007's scope: 26 files across test/config, test/release, test/unit, test/orchestrator, test/transcript, test/issues, test/vendor, test/plan, test/notify, test/logging, test/interactivity, test/fixtures, test/domain-docs, test/retry -- test/retry's MIT headers must survive byte-for-byte per the curated invariant, and its awaited `await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(...))` form needs the same synchronous createTestTmpdir call (works fine under await). GOTCHA 11 (test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts budget) belongs to US-007: raising that budget is explicitly forbidden as a fix, only the migration itself resolves it. The codemod itself is now proven against 4 distinct false-positive/false-negative edge shapes across US-003/US-004/US-006; US-007 should still typecheck immediately after running it as the cheap backstop, but no NEW edge shape is expected barring a fifth quoting pathology.
